questions.question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, you should:

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
Ignore it and keep driving.
Flash your high beams at the driver.
Cut them off to get back at them.

questions.explanation: Do not take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Ignore it and drive safely. This helps you avoid road rage and dangerous situations.

questions.question: Worn or bald tires:

options.text: Can make turning more difficult.
Are more likely to hydroplane.
Can increase your stopping distance.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase stopping distance, make turning harder, and increase the risk of hydroplaning on wet roads.

questions.question: To practice defensive driving, you should:

options.text: Be aware of developing traffic situations around you.
Look ahead of your vehicle and maintain proper following distance.
Have a backup plan ready if something unexpected happens.
All of the above

questions.explanation: Be a defensive driver by looking ahead, anticipating traffic problems, and always having a backup plan. Maintain proper distance and speed for road conditions.

questions.question: You are driving on a four-lane highway behind a slow vehicle. Before changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Signal for at least 100 feet.
Check your blind spot.
Make sure there is enough space to move safely.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check mirrors and look over your shoulder to clear your blind spot. Signal at least 100 feet before you move. Do not cut into a space that would interfere with other drivers' safe distance.

questions.question: A seat belt should be adjusted so that it:

options.text: Is loose.
Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Is hidden beneath the seat.
Stops the seat belt buzzer or light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: Lap belts should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. Shoulder belts should be comfortable with room for one fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden last-minute turn into an exit. If you pass your exit, continue to the next one.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Signal the lane change.
Check your rearview and outside mirrors.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always signal your lane change well in advance, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving.

questions.question: On a multilane highway, you must signal before changing lanes:

options.text: Right before you change lanes.
Only during the lane change.
At least 50 feet before you start.
At least 100 feet before you start.

questions.correctAnswerText: At least 100 feet before you start.
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet (about five car lengths) before changing lanes or turning. Signal for a longer distance at higher speeds.

questions.question: If stopped by a police officer, you should:

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Get your paperwork ready before the officer arrives.
Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
Get out and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel and stay in your vehicle. Tell passengers to keep their hands visible. Do not get out unless the officer asks you to. Wait for the officer to ask for your license, registration, and insurance.

questions.question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, you must produce:

options.text: Proof of insurance.
Your license.
Proof of registration.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You must have your license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance in your vehicle at all times. You must show all three when stopped by police.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the flagger's directions.
Do what other drivers are doing, even if it goes against the flagger's instructions.
Assume the flagger should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal traffic laws instead of the flagger's directions.

questions.explanation: Be ready to slow down and be careful when a sign, flagger, or police officer tells you to. Not following their directions is illegal and unsafe for construction workers.

questions.question: A driver who is taking a non-prescription drug should:

options.text: Read the label before driving.
Drink alcohol instead.
Keep driving no matter what the warning label says.
Drive only during the day.

questions.explanation: Over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving. Check the label for warnings about cold or allergy medicine. If you are not sure, ask your doctor or pharmacist if it is safe to drive while taking the medicine.

questions.question: On a freeway, you realize you missed your turn or exit. You should:

options.text: Make the turn quickly from your current lane.
Stop and back up.
Keep driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or safe place to turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or safe place to turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Go to the next turn or exit where you can safely turn around. Backing up on a freeway shoulder is illegal.

questions.question: If one of your tires blows out while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Brake hard right away.
Keep the steering wheel straight and slowly take your foot off the gas pedal.
Keep your current speed and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to warn the traffic behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the steering wheel straight and slowly take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel tightly and keep the car straight. Remove your foot from the gas pedal slowly. Do not brake until you have full control. When the car is stable, brake gently and pull safely off the road.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, a driver should:

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the accident site.
Not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: If you are in an accident, you must stop at or near the scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if you can. Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes because another car might hit you. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: Drivers who eat and drink while driving:

options.text: Do not make any driving errors.
Have trouble driving slowly.
Are better drivers because they are not hungry.
Have trouble controlling their vehicles.

questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These actions take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. Drivers doing these things have trouble staying in their lanes and controlling their cars.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Your road ends ahead.
You must turn either right or left.
A four-way intersection is ahead.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must turn either right or left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a Y intersection ahead. You must turn either right or left.

questions.question: When you need to change lanes, it is important to:

options.text: Signal before you change lanes.
Check your blind spot.
Make sure the lane is clear before you move into it.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes or exiting. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before you move.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, parking, or entering traffic from an alley or parking area. This tells other drivers what you are doing and helps prevent accidents.

questions.question: What might happen when alcohol is combined with another drug?

options.text: The effects of both the alcohol and the drug may become stronger.
Nothing will happen.
The effects of both the alcohol and the drug may become weaker.
Only the alcohol's effects may become weaker.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both the alcohol and the drug may become stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make both effects stronger. For example, one drink while taking a cold medicine could affect you like having several drinks.

questions.question: If you change your name, you must notify the county examiner of drivers within what timeframe?

options.text: 60 days
20 days
10 days
30 days

questions.explanation: You must tell the county examiner of drivers about a name change in person within 30 days. Bring proof of the change.

questions.question: An intersection has no traffic signs or signals. You arrive at the same time as a vehicle to your right. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and go through the intersection
Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right
Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop
Honk your horn and drive through the intersection

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Let it pass first, then you may go.

questions.question: When you see a steady red traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Drive through if there is no crossing traffic
Continue driving because you have the right-of-way
Stop only if a police officer is nearby
Come to a complete stop

questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop completely. Driving through a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on a red light only if a sign does not forbid it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not drink and drive
Slippery when wet
Road curves ahead
A hill is coming

questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that the road becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: Why is night driving more difficult than daytime driving?

options.text: Cars overheat faster at night
You cannot see as far in the dark
It rains more at night
You see more motorcycles at night

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far in the dark
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see very far. Always use your headlights. Drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Left turn yield on green
One-way street
Cattle crossing
Two-way left turn lane

questions.explanation: This sign means you can turn left on a green light, but you must yield to oncoming traffic. Complete your turn only when it is safe.

questions.question: When you see other drivers acting angrily, what should you do?

options.text: Avoid making eye contact
Do not make hand gestures
Move away from the situation
Do all of these

questions.explanation: Stay away from angry drivers. Avoid eye contact and hand gestures. Slow down, move over, or do whatever you can to stay safe.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light
Keep going because you have the right-of-way
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection
Check what the cars next to you are doing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection
questions.explanation: A yellow light means red is coming next. Stop unless you are already inside the intersection.

questions.question: What does a red and white triangular sign at an intersection mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is coming
Look both ways as you cross
Always come to a full stop
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed
questions.explanation: This is a yield sign. Slow down as you approach and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. Be ready to stop if necessary.

questions.question: How should you safely cross railroad tracks?

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light is flashing
Listen, look both ways, then cross if it is safe
Cross quickly when a train is coming
Pass quickly under lowering gates

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen, look both ways, then cross if it is safe
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are dangerous. Listen and look both directions for trains before crossing. Wait for any warning signals to stop, then only cross when you are sure it is safe.
